script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Psychological
Theme: ambition

Begin screenplay.

Title: THE REMORSEFUL

INT. OFFICE BUILDING - DAY

A modern office building buzzes with activity. People walk quickly, heads down, focused on their phones.

INT. MAX'S OFFICE - DAY

MAX, a driven and ambitious businessman in his late 30s, sits behind a massive oak desk. He wears a crisp shirt, a red power tie, and a satisfied smile.

MAX
(to himself)
Another deal closed. I'm unstoppable.

The phone rings.

MAX
Yes?

NARRATOR (V.O.)
Max Schultz, a man of immense ambition, had finally arrived at the pinnacle of success. But at what cost?

EXT. CITY PARK - DAY

Max walks through the park, a serene oasis in the midst of the urban jungle. He sits on a bench, seemingly lost in thought.

MAX
(to himself)
I need a break.

INT. MAX'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Max enters his sleek, minimalist apartment. He pours himself a glass of scotch and sits at the kitchen table. The phone rings again.

MAX
Hello?

An UNKNOWN VOICE speaks on the other end.

UNKNOWN VOICE
(sinister)
Mr. Schultz, I've been watching you...

INT. MAX'S OFFICE - DAY

Max sits at his desk, visibly shaken. He checks his phone for a missed call but finds none.

MAX
Who was that?

NARRATOR (V.O.)
Max, once a confident and fearless man, now finds himself plagued by paranoia and fear.

INT. MAX'S THERAPIST'S OFFICE - NIGHT

Max sits across from DR. SILVER, a kind and understanding therapist.

MAX
(distressed)
I've been getting these strange phone calls. I think someone's following me.

DR. SILVER
(sensitively)
Max, I believe you, but we need to find evidence. Are there any patterns to these calls?

INT. MAX'S OFFICE - NIGHT

Max reviews the call logs on his phone, but he finds no patterns. He begins to doubt himself.

MAX
I must be going crazy.

INT. MAX'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Max sets up hidden cameras in his apartment, convinced that someone is watching him. He checks them repeatedly, but they show nothing.

MAX
(to himself)
This is ridiculous. I need to focus on my business.

INT. MAX'S OFFICE - DAY

Max closes a major deal, but his mind is preoccupied with the mysterious phone calls and the fear that someone is stalking him.

MAX
(to himself)
I can't let this affect my work.

INT. MAX'S THERAPIST'S OFFICE - NIGHT

Max tells Dr. Silver about the latest developments.

MAX
I think it's getting worse. I can't shake this feeling of being watched.

DR. SILVER
Max, it's important that we don't let fear control us. We need to find the source of these calls.

INT. MAX'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Max receives another call, but this time he answers. It's an old acquaintance, JESSICA.

JESSICA
(surprised)
Max! I didn't expect to hear from you.

MAX
(suspicious)
Why have you been calling me?

JESSICA
(confused)
I haven't. I've been trying to reach out to you for weeks, but you never replied.

Max realizes that he's been living in fear of a threat that doesn't exist. He apologizes to Jessica and invites her over for a drink.

INT. MAX'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Max and Jessica catch up, laughing and sharing old memories. Max begins to relax, grateful for the reminder of the connections he's made throughout his life.

MAX
(smiling)
I've been so focused on my ambition that I forgot about the people in my life.

NARRATOR (V.O.)
Max Schultz, a man once consumed by his own ambition, has found redemption in the connections he's made along the way.

INT. MAX'S OFFICE - DAY

Max returns to work, no longer plagued by fear. He closes yet another deal, but this time, he shares the success with his colleagues and even takes Jessica out for a celebratory dinner.

MAX
(to himself)
I've arrived, but I'm not alone.

FADE OUT.

End of screenplay.
